# History rewrite, 2026-11-05

At the owner's request, a personal corporate e-mail address that this Mac's global git configuration had put on 86
commits (85 as author and committer, 1 as committer) and on 3 release tags (v0.12.1, v0.12.2, v0.12.3, as tagger) was
replaced with the owner's personal address, `heet1356@gmail.com`.

**What changed.** Only identity metadata. Each rewritten commit has the same tree, message, author and committer names
and dates as before (checked for all 513); only the e-mail field differs. The rewrite was limited to those commits and
their descendants, so the 230 older commits, including every commit and tag up to v0.11.3, keep their SHAs and
GitHub signatures. 513 commit SHAs changed, among them the merge commits GitHub had signed after the first affected
commit (rewriting drops those signatures).

**Tags.** v0.11.5 through v0.12.6 (12 tags) now point at the rewritten commits; each points at the same file tree as
before. The three tags with the old tagger were re-created with the same message and date. PyPI packages and GitHub
release files are unchanged (no build was redone). The build-provenance attestations of those releases name the
original commit SHA; use the map below to find the rewritten commit.

**Branches.** `main` was force-pushed once, with branch protection lifted for that push only and then restored to the
same settings (and the release and CI workflows disabled while the tags moved, so nothing was republished). The 160
merged branches were deleted; one open pull request branch was replayed onto the new `main`.

**Not covered.** GitHub keeps read-only pull-request refs and cached pages that still show the old commits until
GitHub Support purges them; the owner was given the request text.

**SHA map.** Every SHA cited elsewhere in `docs/engineering/` before this date may be an old one: look it up here.
`old new`, newest first.
